title: Parochial school bands and private teachers Buech, Kruger and Rudy Wiedoeft
summary: His school had little music program, so he studied privately with Arthur Buech, Arthur Kruger and Walker, plus a couple of lessons with Rudy Wiedoeft.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That's very nice. Was there any connection to any formal or academic music education in your school?

No, not the school I attended. Where I spent most of my years was at St. John's Cathedral Grade School and then later high school, and there was not -- they had a semblance of a band program, but not very much. But I was called upon to play constantly while I was a member of that grouping in school.
And I kept studying with private teachers, people like Arthur Buech.

B-u-e-c-h. And another man by the name of Arthur Kruger. And they were both very fine. And actually, later I took some lessons from a man by the name of [Veesee] Walker, whose son was here in California and has been for a number of years, I believe, and he was music director and head of the band program at USC for a number of years, Tom Walker.

And at one point, I guess maybe when I was about 12, 13, I managed to get a couple of very instructive periods with Rudy Weedoff when he was touring and happened to be in Milwaukee. And it was arranged for me to have a couple of hours with him. And I think he taught me a great deal.
